olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers. The cells of an
$$(a+b+1)\times(a+b+1)$$
grid are colored amber and bronze such that there are at least
$$a^2+ab-b$$
amber cells and at least
$$b^2+ab-a$$
bronze cells. Prove that it is possible to choose $a$ amber cells and $b$ bronze cells such that no two of the $a+b$ chosen cells lie in the same row or column.
figure_description: Colored grid selection problem with row/column restrictions.
statement_note: Grid-size and counting expressions visually verified from official PDF because OCR partially corrupted exponents and subtraction signs. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $b\ge2$ and $w\ge2$ be fixed integers, and let
$$n=b+w.$$
Given are $2b$ identical black rods and $2w$ identical white rods, each of side length $1$.

We assemble a regular $2n$-gon using these rods so that parallel sides are the same color. Then, a convex $2b$-gon $B$ is formed by translating the black rods, and a convex $2w$-gon $W$ is formed by translating the white rods.

Prove that the difference of the areas of $B$ and $W$ depends only on the numbers $b$ and $w$, and not on how the $2n$-gon was assembled.
figure_description: Assembly of a regular polygon from colored rods producing two convex polygons.
statement_note: Polygon notation and construction visually verified from official PDF including embedded diagram. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let
$$\mathbb{R}_{>0}$$
be the set of all positive real numbers. Find all functions
$$f:\mathbb{R}_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$$
such that for all
$$x,y\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}$$
we have
$$
f(x)=f(f(f(x))+y)+f(xf(y))f(x+y).
$$
statement_note: Nested functional-equation expression visually verified from official PDF because OCR partially corrupted parentheses. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Find all pairs of primes $(p,q)$ for which
$$p-q$$
and
$$pq-q$$
are both perfect squares.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
A function
$$f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$$
is essentially increasing if
$$f(s)\le f(t)$$
holds whenever
$$s\le t$$
are real numbers such that
$$f(s)\ne0$$
and
$$f(t)\ne0.$$

Find the smallest integer $k$ such that for any $2022$ real numbers
$$x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{2022},$$
there exist $k$ essentially increasing functions
$$f_1,\ldots,f_k$$
such that
$$
f_1(n)+f_2(n)+\cdots+f_k(n)=x_n
$$
for every
$$n=1,2,\ldots,2022.$$
statement_note: Definition and summation notation visually verified from official PDF because OCR partially corrupted inequalities and subscripts. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
There are $2022$ users on a social network called Mathbook, and some of them are Mathbook-friends. (On Mathbook, friendship is always mutual and permanent.)

Starting now, Mathbook will only allow a new friendship to be formed between two users if they have at least two friends in common. What is the minimum number of friendships that must already exist so that every user could eventually become friends with every other user?
figure_description: Friendship-expansion process on a social network graph.
